# Copilot Instructions for `barsource`

## Build, test, and lint commands

This repo has two Dart packages (`dart/` and `example/`) plus a native C++ backend (`native/`).

### Dart package (`dart/`)

```bash
cd dart
dart pub get
dart analyze
dart test
```

Run a single test file:

```bash
cd dart
dart test test/<file_name>_test.dart
```

Run a single test by name:

```bash
cd dart
dart test -n "<test name substring>"
```

### Example package (`example/`)

```bash
cd example
dart pub get
dart analyze
dart test
```

Run a single test file:

```bash
cd example
dart test test/<file_name>_test.dart
```

### Native backend (`native/`)

```bash
cd native
cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build -- -j$(nproc)
```

### End-to-end local render run

From repo root:

```bash
./run_script.sh
```

This script builds native code, copies produced shared libraries into `dart/lib/blob/`, then runs `dart run` in `example/`.

### Regenerate Dart FFI bindings after changing native headers

```bash
cd dart
dart run ffigen
```

## High-level architecture

- Public Dart API entrypoint is `dart/lib/src/engine/render_controller.dart` (`render(...)`), which initializes `Engine`, runs rendering, then shuts it down.
- `Engine` (`dart/lib/src/engine/engine.dart`) is the orchestration core. It mixes in:
  - `SchedulerBinding` (frame callback phases),
  - `WidgetsBinding` (widget/element build pipeline),
  - `RendererBinding` (render tree + layout/paint flushing),
  - `AudioBinding` (audio contributor/decoder integration).
- Rendering model is offline frame generation (not a realtime UI app loop). `Engine.run(...)` advances its own timeline, builds/layouts/paints, writes video frame + audio samples to native encoder each frame.
- Widget system and element tree are Flutter-inspired but custom (`dart/lib/src/widgets/*`, `dart/lib/src/elements/framework.dart`), and produce custom render objects (`dart/lib/src/rendering/*`).
- Native integration is through FFI bindings (`dart/lib/src/engine/bindings.dart`) generated from `native/include/tennoji/engine.h`; implementation is in `native/src/` and built by CMake.
- `example/` is the primary integration usage sample and demonstrates animation, media clips, and timeline-driven state updates via `EngineTimer`.

## Key conventions specific to this codebase

- Barrel files in `dart/lib/*.dart` are generated by `dart/barrel_gen.py` and marked `AUTO-GENERATED BARREL FILE. DO NOT EDIT BY HAND`. Update source files under `dart/lib/src/**` and regenerate barrels instead of hand-editing exports.
- The intended high-level API is `render(widget, RenderConfig)`; avoid bypassing it unless you are intentionally changing engine lifecycle behavior.
- Render object durations drive timeline behavior. Sequence/timeline composition depends on `RenderObject.duration`, `TimelineParentData`, and `Sequence`/`RenderSequence` logic rather than external schedulers.
- Audio is tree-composed via `AudioContributor` mixin; contributors collect descendant audio, optionally add own samples, then post-process. Preserve this subtree mixing model when adding audio effects/clips.
- Native artifact bundling for Dart uses the hook in `dart/hook/build.dart` and expects platform libraries in `dart/lib/blob/` (`libtennoji.so`, `libtennoji.dylib`, or `tennoji.dll`).
- The root render attachment is done through `RootWidget`/`RootElement` (`dart/lib/src/widgets/root.dart`), which intentionally bypasses normal ancestor render-object attachment for the render tree root.
- The render loop and many image/media operations are intentionally synchronous for deterministic frame-by-frame output.
